rawOutput.rationale: Build the WWI cause map in prerequisite order with two teach-and-check cycles: alliances and tensions first, then the Sarajevo-to-war sequence, then a closing chronology retrieval. This matches the novice starting point, the self-explanation method, and the 45-minute pacing while keeping deferred future content out of the session.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions created a divided European system with rival alliance blocs and rising pressure before 1914.
The Sarajevo assassination set off the July Crisis, where ultimata, mobilization, and alliance commitments widened the conflict into declarations of war.
From 1914 to 1918, World War I moved from outbreak to U.S. entry and then to the armistice in 1918.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a model of the WWI cause map, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, and explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining the chain of causes and events helps make the war story coherent and exposes missing links.
how: Study one concise model of the cause map.
Close it and explain the main relationships in plain language.
Compare your explanation with the model and repair any gap.
methodBriefing.completion: You can state the main relationships clearly, repair a gap, and reexplain the full idea.
personalization: Start with the whole picture before details.
Use one concrete example before abstraction.
Keep one step visible at a time.

activities.label: Model the alliance map
activities.title: Europe before 1914
activities.body: Read the model and notice the main division first.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions created a divided European system with rival alliance blocs and rising pressure before 1914.

activities.label: Explain the cause map
activities.title: What set off the war?
activities.body: Explain the cause chain in your own words. Then compare it to the model.
activities.correctAnswer: The alliances and tensions split Europe into rival blocs, and the Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis that spread through ultimata, mobilization, and alliance commitments into war.
activities.feedback: A complete answer links the prewar tensions to the outbreak sequence. If needed, repair missing parts by naming the alliance blocs and the escalation steps after Sarajevo.

activities.label: Repair the explanation
activities.title: Fix the missing link
activities.body: Use the hint to correct your explanation. Then try again in one clear sentence.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The assassination alone caused the war, with no important role for alliance commitments or mobilization.
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination started the July Crisis, but alliance commitments and mobilization helped turn it into a wider war.
activities.feedback: The key correction is that Sarajevo began the crisis, not the entire war by itself. Include the wider escalation step.

activities.label: Reexplain the timeline
activities.title: WWI from start to end
activities.body: Give the timeline from start to finish without copying the model.
activities.correctAnswer: Sarajevo in 1914, the July Crisis, the start of the war in 1914, U.S. entry in 1917, and the armistice in 1918.
activities.feedback: A correct timeline keeps the events in order and ends with the armistice. If you missed one step, add it without changing the sequence.

activities.label: Check the full sequence
activities.title: Pick the best summary
activities.body: Choose the summary that best matches the cause map.
choices: Rival alliances and tensions shaped Europe before 1914, Sarajevo triggered the July Crisis, war began in 1914, the United States entered in 1917, and the armistice came in 1918.
The war began in 1918 after the armistice, and Sarajevo happened after U.S. entry.
The assassination directly ended the war in 1914, and the armistice came before the U.S. entry.
Europe had no major tensions before 1914, so the war started only because of one isolated event.
activities.correctAnswer: Rival alliances and tensions shaped Europe before 1914, Sarajevo triggered the July Crisis, war began in 1914, the United States entered in 1917, and the armistice came in 1918.
activities.feedback: This summary matches the overall timeline and the escalation path from Sarajevo to war. The other choices scramble the chronology or ignore the prewar tensions.

check.referenceAnswer: They divided Europe into hostile, militarized alliance blocs, increasing suspicion and the risk that a local crisis would spread.
